metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: Data available from the corresponding author upon request.

hyperparameters.name: Learning rate (eta)
hyperparameters.context: Parameter used in Adam optimizer for weight updates.

hyperparameters.name: Batch size (k)
hyperparameters.context: Number of transitions sampled from replay buffer for training.

hyperparameters.name: Replay buffer size (B)
hyperparameters.context: Maximum number of experience transitions stored for training.

hyperparameters.name: Decision step size (L)
hyperparameters.context: Fixed time interval for the agent to determine the signal phase.

hyperparameters.name: Exploration rate (epsilon)
hyperparameters.context: Probability of selecting a random action to explore policies.

hyperparameters.name: Freeze interval (F)
hyperparameters.context: Frequency of updating the target network weights by copying.

hyperparameters.name: Reward weight (mu)
hyperparameters.context: Weight for the speed component in the reward calculation.

hyperparameters.name: Reward weight (omega)
hyperparameters.context: Weight for the queue length component in the reward calculation.

metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volume and behavior data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters in the SUMO simulator.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The Data Availability statement explicitly states that the data used to support the results are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts (xi, yi) coordinates for each vehicle in a control area of size X by Y. Vehicles are represented as points in a matrix mt.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, generic tool implied, required parameters described conceptually.

nodes_process.source_quote: After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4 x 512 in pixels. Three consecutive observations are stacked
nodes_process.description: Constructs the state st by stacking N consecutive position matrices after down-sampling to a 4x512 resolution. Includes signal state (red/green) as specific matrix elements.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, stack size and dimensions fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a Q-network using Adam optimizer. Implements experience replay, target networks, and multitask learning to predict mean speed and queue length alongside Q-values.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named (SUMO), all required hyperparameters provided in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained DRL policy against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines using 20 simulation experiments based on real-world traffic volumes.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulation tool and parameters (time, speeds, decision steps) fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Removes information from specific subareas (1-8) of the control area to test the DRL controller's sensitivity to spatial video data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, experiment design clearly mapped in Fig 15, subarea count stated.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 6 presents the 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal distribution of traffic volumes used in simulation for both mainline and on-ramp.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Empirical traffic data provided via graph but not raw file; simulation settings in SUMO described.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Training convergence of the DRL agent showing reward and travel time over 1 million frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Hyperparameters and hardware specified; requires proprietary empirical data for exact match.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline travel time comparison between No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL across the peak period.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Methods for baselines and DRL are specified; results derive directly from simulation outputs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Statistical comparison of mean travel times for 20 experimental runs across three control methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Explicit numerical results for multiple runs provided; dependent on SUMO environment calibration.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of speed in (a) no-control; (b) PI-ALINEA; (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing traffic speed as a function of distance and time along the freeway mainline.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plausible aggregation of simulation telemetry; distance/time scales clearly labeled.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Boxplots of traffic volume downstream of the merge area for the three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison of throughput; follows directly from simulation logs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis of DRL performance (travel time) relative to spatial information loss.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure for perturbing input matrices is well-defined; results support the visual data claim.
